newsitem.title: FRANCE: France fears no compromise with U.S. on NATO post.
newsitem.headline: France fears no compromise with U.S. on NATO post.

text.p: Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Sunday France might fail to persuade Washington to let a European officer take over NATO's southern command from an American.
De Charette, in a late-night television interview, said the two countries were seeking ways to settle the dispute which has been deadlocked for months.
He was asked what type of compromise might be possible.

"We'll see. Diplomats are working to see if a compromise is possible. As you know, President (Bill) Clinton and President (Jacques) Chirac spoke by telephone a few days ago," he said, referring to a 30-minute call on Thursday.
"We are exchanging missions. We're working. If it's possible then that's good. If it's not possible, well...we'll leave it at that."
His comments, apparently playing down the dispute, were a far cry from a letter Chirac wrote to Clinton in Ocbober, insisting that the issue was of "capital importance" to Paris.

Washington on Tuesday publicly rejected a French compromise proposal to split the Naples-based command, giving a U.S. admiral control over air-naval protection forces and a European territorial responsibility.

France, planning to make a full return to NATO's military command which it quit in 1966, wants a European officer to head NATO's southern command as part of a drive to give European nations greater responsibility for their own defence.
The Naples-based command controls allied forces in the Mediterranean including Bosnia.
In September, French Defence Minister Charles Millon threatened to freeze France's reintegration into NATO's military structure if it failed to get its way. Officials have not repeated that threat.
